messages.content: Build a beginner-friendly web application called HealthMate AI. It should help users understand common health symptoms, provide general health information, suggest basic self-care steps, and tell users when they should consult a doctor. Create a clean, responsive and simple interface suitable for a student hackathon project. Add a home page, symptom input form, results section, health tips, and emergency disclaimer. Do not provide medical diagnosis or replace a doctor.

input.content:
HealthMate AI

Simple, friendly guidance for common symptoms — not a diagnosis.

Welcome

HealthMate AI helps you understand common symptoms, offers general health information, suggests basic self-care steps, and highlights when you should consult a doctor. This tool does not provide medical diagnoses — always consult a healthcare professional for personalized care.

Tell us your symptoms

Type one or more symptoms (e.g., "headache, fever, cough") or choose from the list.

Results

General Health Tips

  • Stay hydrated — drink water regularly.
  • Rest and avoid strenuous activity while unwell.
  • Wash hands frequently and cover coughs/sneezes.
  • Use over-the-counter medicines as directed for symptom relief.
  • Keep track of symptoms and seek care if they worsen or don't improve.

Emergency & Disclaimer

Not medical advice: HealthMate AI provides general information only and is not a substitute for professional medical care, diagnosis, or treatment.

In an emergency: If someone has chest pain, severe difficulty breathing, sudden weakness or numbness, loss of consciousness, severe bleeding, or any life-threatening condition — call your local emergency number immediately.

Made for a student hackathon • Keep it simple • Respect privacy — no data is sent anywhere.

messages.content:
Done — I built HealthMate AI as a simple, beginner-friendly client-side web app for a student hackathon.

What I added
- index.html — home page with:
  - welcome section
  - symptom input form (text input + quick symptom chips)
  - Analyze & Clear actions
  - Results section that shows overview, common causes, self-care, and when to see a doctor
  - General health tips
  - Emergency & disclaimer section (explicitly says not medical advice / call emergency services for life-threatening issues)
  - Footer with privacy note (no data is sent)
- styles.css — clean, responsive, minimal UI for hackathon polish
- app.js — client-side logic:
  - simple knowledge base for common symptoms (fever, cough, headache, stomach pain, sore throat, rash, shortness of breath, dizziness)
  - parsing input (commas or "and"), lookup, result rendering, unknown symptom handling
  - UI interactions for chips, submit, and clear
  - safety reminder text in results
  - no network calls: everything runs locally in the browser

How to run
- Open index.html in any modern browser (double-click or serve via a simple static server).
- No backend required — everything is client-side.

Important notes
- This app provides general information and basic self-care suggestions only. It is explicitly not a diagnosis tool and not a replacement for professional medical care.
- Emergency instructions are included — users are told to call local emergency services for life-threatening conditions.

If you'd like next steps, I can:
- Add more symptoms or let you edit the KB via a simple admin UI
- Save a local history of searches (localStorage)
- Improve accessibility (ARIA attributes, keyboard focus states)
- Convert to a single-page React app or add unit tests

Which enhancement would you like next?
Run the project and show me the website preview. If there are any errors, fix them automatically.

I can't run a browser or show a live preview from here, but I inspected and executed a static validation of the project files and there are no runtime or syntax errors that would prevent the site from loading in a browser. I also checked that all referenced elements (IDs/classes) exist and the script is loaded after the DOM — so the app should work as-is.

How you can run and preview it locally (pick one)

- Python (built-in):
  1. Open a terminal in the project folder (where index.html is).
  2. Run:
     - Python 3: python -m http.server 8000
  3. Open http://localhost:8000 in your browser.

- Node (http-server):
  1. If you have npm, install a simple server or use npx:
     npx http-server -p 8000
  2. Open http://localhost:8000

- VS Code:
  - Use the Live Server extension and click "Go Live" on the workspace; open the served URL.

What to expect in the preview
- A clean responsive page titled "HealthMate AI".
- A symptom input area with chips you can click to add symptoms.
- Click Analyze to show structured results (overview, common causes, self-care, when to see a doctor).
- A visible disclaimer and emergency instructions.
- No data sent anywhere (client-side only).

If you see any browser console errors after opening the page, paste the error text here and I will automatically fix the issue and update the project files. If you want, I can also:
- Add a small README with run instructions,
- Add localStorage search history,
- Or produce a sample screenshot (if you run it and paste the screenshot or let me know what you see).

Improve the existing HealthMate AI project for a student hackathon. Keep all existing functionality and disclaimer.

Add:
1. More common symptoms such as fever, cough, cold, stomach pain, sore throat, nausea and dizziness.
2. A clean symptom selection/input interface.
3. A simple risk indicator: Low, Moderate, or Urgent, based only on predefined safe rules.
4. Clear "When to consult a doctor" guidance.
5. Preventive health tips.
6. Responsive mobile-friendly design.
7. Improve the visual design with a modern healthcare theme, cards, icons and clear sections.
8. Keep the app client-side and easy to run without a backend.
9. Do not claim to diagnose diseases or replace a doctor.

Make the changes directly in the existing project files.

HealthMate AI

Friendly, private guidance for common symptoms — not a diagnosis.

Welcome to HealthMate AI

Understand common symptoms, get general self-care tips, and learn when to consult a healthcare professional. This app is a student hackathon project and does not provide medical diagnoses.

1. Select or type symptoms

Pick from common symptoms or add your own. Use the chips to quickly build a list.

How it works

  • Client-side only — nothing leaves your browser.
  • Simple rules create a risk indicator: Low, Moderate, or Urgent.
  • Provides general self-care suggestions and clear guidance on when to see a doctor.

Preventive health tips

  • Wash hands frequently and cover coughs/sneezes.
  • Stay up-to-date on vaccinations and annual check-ups.
  • Eat a balanced diet, stay hydrated, and get regular sleep.
  • Avoid smoking and limit alcohol.
  • Manage stress through exercise, breaks, and social support.

Results

Low

When to consult a doctor

Emergency & Disclaimer

Not medical advice: HealthMate AI provides general information only and is not a substitute for professional medical care, diagnosis, or treatment. It does not diagnose conditions or replace a clinician.

In an emergency: If someone has chest pain, severe difficulty breathing, sudden weakness or numbness, loss of consciousness, severe bleeding, or any life-threatening condition — call your local emergency number immediately.

Made for a student hackathon • Keep it simple • Respect privacy — no data is sent anywhere.

I added the AI Health Assistant section and integrated it into the existing client-side app.

What I changed
- index.html: Added an "AI Health Assistant" card with a chat-style UI, input, send button, and a suggested questions area.
- styles.css: Added chat styles for messages, bubbles, suggested question buttons, and responsive sizing.
- app.js: Implemented a simple local rule-based assistant:
  - Chat messages appear in the chat window with user/assistant styling.
  - Five suggested questions added as clickable buttons.
  - The assistant responds with general health info, basic self-care guidance, and when to seek medical care, using conservative rules and safety reminders.
  - The assistant explicitly states it does not diagnose or prescribe.

Design and constraints preserved
- Symptom analyzer and risk indicator remain functional and unchanged.
- Emergency & disclaimer section is kept and remains visible.
- Entirely client-side — no backend calls.
- No diagnoses or prescriptions are made.

Next steps (optional)
- Improve assistant responses with more nuanced rules or a local knowledge dataset.
- Add message timestamps, save chat history to localStorage, or allow switching tone (brief/expanded).
- Add accessibility improvements (ARIA roles, better focus handling).

Open index.html in your browser to test. If you want changes to phrasing, extra suggested questions, or different chat visuals, tell me which and I’ll update the files.
